NAViECO · Layer 0¶

Reference-guided hierarchical cell-type annotation | Complete Jupyter tutorial¶

Version: NAViECO 0.1.0a2 · GitHub commit e3bb5dc
Source: github.com/LuckyRaphael/NAViECO
Kernel: Python 3.11 (NAViECO v0.1.0a2)

Annotate an entire single-cell RNA-seq dataset with the published NAViECO_v1 reference. This notebook keeps the editable settings in one cell and performs only one annotation/training run. Everything afterward reads the results without fitting new models.

Input: a raw-count .h5ad file (cells × genes), unique cell/gene identifiers, and an optional sample/batch column in adata.obs. Raw counts must be in adata.layers["counts"] (preferred) or adata.X.
Output: one annotated .h5ad, hierarchical labels/confidences, three-stage training diagnostics, and publication-ready PDF reports. No downsampling is performed by this notebook.

Run on a compute node with enough RAM and preferably a compatible GPU—not on an HPC login node. Public Layer 0 provides cell types, not the cell-state recovery (Layer 1) or multicellular modules (later layers) planned for NAViECO.

1 · Configure your data and run¶

Edit only the settings marked # EDIT. Use an absolute path if the Notebook and data are in different directories. SAMPLE_KEY is the exact column name in adata.obs, not a cell barcode, a sample ID value, or a separate sample_id= argument.

Setting What to enter Example
INPUT_H5AD Full path to the complete, raw-count Query .h5ad /data/my_cohort.h5ad
OUTPUT_DIR Directory where results should be saved /data/NAViECO_output
SAMPLE_KEY Exact .obs column identifying each sample or batch "sample_id", "sample", "orig.ident"
LEVEL "fine" = Levels 1–3; "coarse" = Levels 1–2 "fine"
DEVICE "auto" (detect CUDA), "cuda", or "cpu" "auto"

Important: Multiple cells belonging to the same biological sample should have the same sample ID. Different samples should not inadvertently share an ID (including across cohorts). Set SAMPLE_KEY=None only if an explicit sample column is not appropriate; NAViECO then uses .obs["Dataset"] if available, otherwise treats Query as a single domain. It does not automatically detect a sample_id column.

In [3]:
from pathlib import Path
from importlib.metadata import version
import sys
import anndata as ad
import navieco as nv
from IPython.display import display

# ── Required: edit for YOUR new dataset ───────────────────────────────
INPUT_H5AD = Path("/charite-store-f/f-bih-pancan_icb_atlas_2026/6.scRNA_Recovery1/6.0.Metadata_test/PMID42679812_3cohorts_subset.h5ad")   # EDIT: raw-count .h5ad
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("/charite-store-f/f-bih-pancan_icb_atlas_2026/6.scRNA_Recovery1/6.1.NAViECO_Layer0_user_test/output")  # EDIT: save location
SAMPLE_KEY = "sample"                                 # EDIT: .obs column; or None

# ── Recommended defaults ─────────────────────────────────────────────
REFERENCE = "NAViECO_v1"
LEVEL = "fine"              # fine: Levels 1–3; coarse: Levels 1–2
DEVICE = "auto"             # auto / cuda / cpu
RUN_UMAP = True             # compute UMAPs and export annotation/UMAP PDFs
N_HVG = 3000                # Query HVGs, combined with frozen Reference HVGs
BATCH_SIZE = 128            # model training mini-batch; NOT the sample ID
ADVANCED = None             # None = package defaults; see the settings table below

RESULT_H5AD = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{INPUT_H5AD.stem}_NAViECO_{LEVEL}.h5ad"

if not INPUT_H5AD.is_file():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Edit INPUT_H5AD: file not found: {INPUT_H5AD}")
print(f"NAViECO {version('navieco')} | Python {sys.version.split()[0]}")
print(f"Installed package: {nv.__file__}")
print(f"Input:  {INPUT_H5AD}\nOutput: {RESULT_H5AD}")

2 · Inspect the input (no training)¶

This read uses AnnData backed mode: it checks the input metadata without loading the whole gene-expression matrix into memory. You can identify the correct SAMPLE_KEY from the printed obs columns before fitting models.

  • Cell IDs: adata.obs_names must be unique; NAViECO does not change them.
  • Gene IDs: adata.var_names must be unique. NAViECO harmonizes supported gene names with its reference; you do not need to normalize/log-transform counts first.
  • Counts: if layers["counts"] exists, NAViECO automatically uses it; otherwise, X must contain raw non-negative integer counts. It does not accept a counts_layer= option in the public nv.annotate() interface.
  • Sample IDs: the values under the selected .obs column must be nonempty; a single sample can still contain many cells.

If SAMPLE_KEY is wrong, change it in Step 1, then rerun this inspection cell.

In [4]:
query = ad.read_h5ad(INPUT_H5AD, backed="r")
try:
    print(f"Query: {query.n_obs:,} cells × {query.n_vars:,} genes")
    print("Available obs columns:", list(query.obs.columns))
    print("Raw counts expected in:", 'layers["counts"]' if "counts" in query.layers else "X")
    if not query.obs_names.is_unique or not query.var_names.is_unique:
        raise ValueError("Cell IDs and gene IDs must both be unique.")
    if SAMPLE_KEY is not None:
        if SAMPLE_KEY not in query.obs:
            raise KeyError(f"SAMPLE_KEY={SAMPLE_KEY!r} missing from .obs; choose a listed column.")
        sample_ids = query.obs[SAMPLE_KEY].astype("string").str.strip()
        if sample_ids.isna().any() or sample_ids.eq("").any():
            raise ValueError(f"Missing/blank sample IDs in .obs[{SAMPLE_KEY!r}].")
        print(f"Samples/batches: {sample_ids.nunique():,}")
        display(sample_ids.value_counts().head(10).rename_axis("sample ID").to_frame("cells"))
    else:
        print('SAMPLE_KEY=None: NAViECO will use "Dataset" if present, otherwise one Query domain.')
finally:
    query.file.close()

3 · Load the published NAViECO_v1 reference¶

No manual reference file download or local HPC reference path is needed. The first call below obtains the NAViECO_v1 Reference Release, verifies its published SHA-256 checksum, extracts it, and caches it locally; subsequent calls reuse the verified cache.

The reference contains the seed annotations and frozen, stage-specific HVG resources used for Layer 0. Its hierarchy defines 5 Level 1 lineages, 23 Level 2 cell types, and 129 Level 3 labels. These are the reference label vocabulary sizes; an individual Query may predict fewer observed types.

For an offline installation, set the NAVIECO_REFERENCE_DIR environment variable to an already extracted, valid reference directory before running this cell. Otherwise leave it unset for automatic public download.

In [5]:
reference_dir = nv.get_reference(REFERENCE)
print(f"Reference ready: {reference_dir}")

Reference ready: /home/jizh13/.cache/navieco/references/NAViECO_v1

4 · Run Layer 0 — the only training cell¶

NAViECO trains independent CONCORD classifiers using reference-labelled seed cells; the Query cells are unlabelled during training:

Stage What is learned Fine mode Coarse mode
A · Level 1 One global model predicting 5 broad lineages ✓ ✓
B · Level 2 Separate models within each predicted Level 1 lineage ✓ ✓
C · Level 3 Separate models within each predicted Level 2 parent ✓ —

Only the Query is annotated. Its original count matrix and metadata are preserved in the result. Level 2/3 labels follow the selected parent hierarchy; the corresponding confidences are hierarchical joint probabilities, not independently calibrated Query accuracy.

Training settings (public advanced defaults):

Parameter Default Notes
n_epochs_level1 / latent_dim_level1 15 / 100 Stage A
n_epochs_level2 / latent_dim_level2 15 / 100 Stage B
n_epochs_level3 / latent_dim_level3 15 / 300 Stage C (fine only)
seed 42 Applied to training
n_hvg 2000 Number of Query HVGs; combined with frozen Reference HVGs
batch_size 128 Training mini-batch, unrelated to sample identities

To override the training defaults, replace only ADVANCED = None in Step 1 with, for example:

ADVANCED = {"n_epochs_level1": 20, "n_epochs_level2": 20,
            "n_epochs_level3": 20, "seed": 42}

The saved output is reused if it already exists. That prevents hours of accidental retraining when reopening this Notebook. If you change dataset, SAMPLE_KEY, ADVANCED, or other model settings, choose a new output filename/directory rather than silently reusing the previous result. A completed training run automatically saves its H5AD and all standard reports.

In [6]:
if RESULT_H5AD.exists():
    print(f"Existing result found — loading WITHOUT retraining: {RESULT_H5AD}")
    result = ad.read_h5ad(RESULT_H5AD)
else:
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result = nv.annotate(
        data=str(INPUT_H5AD),
        reference=REFERENCE,
        level=LEVEL,
        batch_key=SAMPLE_KEY,
        n_hvg=N_HVG,
        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        device=DEVICE,
        advanced=ADVANCED,
        run_umap=RUN_UMAP,
        output=str(RESULT_H5AD),
        verbose=True,
    )
print(f"Annotated: {result.n_obs:,} cells × {result.n_vars:,} genes")

5 · Examine annotations, confidences and training records¶
    

  • result.obs["navieco_level1"]: broad lineage.
    • 

  • result.obs["navieco_level2"]: lineage-specific cell type.
    • 

  • result.obs["navieco_level3"]: finer parent-specific cell type (with LEVEL="fine").
    • 

  • navieco_level*_confidence: selected path's prediction confidence. Level 2/3 values include upstream hierarchy probabilities; a lower numerical value does not by itself imply incorrect biology.
    • 

  • nv.training_summary(result): results for every model actually trained, including losses and available held-out Reference validation accuracy. This is not an estimate of prediction accuracy on unlabeled Query cells.
    • 



The numbers of observed cell types may be smaller than 5/23/129 because this dataset need not contain every Reference category.

levels = (1, 2, 3) if LEVEL == "fine" else (1, 2)

    key = f"navieco_level{i}"
    print(f"Level {i}: {result.obs[key].nunique()} observed cell types")
    display(result.obs[key].value_counts().head(10).rename_axis("cell type").to_frame("cells"))

6 · Find the saved results (no additional training)¶
Files are automatically written next to the output H5AD and share its filename prefix:






File suffix
Contents






.h5ad
All Query cells, metadata, hierarchical predictions, probabilities and embeddings




_UMAP.pdf
Same global Level 1 Query UMAP colored by each available label level




_branch_UMAP.pdf
Separate within-lineage Level 2 / within-parent Level 3 projections; branch coordinate systems must not be compared as if shared




_annotation.pdf
All observed cell-type abundances plus confidence distributions; paginated beyond 30 types




_training.pdf
Stage-wise training/validation losses and reference validation accuracy




_training_summary.csv
Model-specific training statistics




_training_metrics.json
Epoch-level history for each trained classifier




_run_config.json
Requested/effective parameters and model metadata






The three UMAP/annotation PDFs require RUN_UMAP=True; the training diagnostics are written whenever output is provided. The reported validation accuracy is calculated using held-out Reference cells, not Query ground truth.


















In [8]:






from IPython.display import FileLink

prefix = RESULT_H5AD.with_suffix("")
expected = [RESULT_H5AD] + [
    prefix.with_name(prefix.name + suffix) for suffix in (
        "_UMAP.pdf", "_branch_UMAP.pdf", "_annotation.pdf", "_training.pdf",
        "_training_summary.csv", "_training_metrics.json", "_run_config.json",
    )
]
for file in expected:
    print(f"{'✓' if file.is_file() else '—'} {file.name}")
print(f"\nAll outputs: {OUTPUT_DIR.resolve()}")
if RESULT_H5AD.exists():
    display(FileLink(str(RESULT_H5AD)))

7 · Optional: per-model training curves (no retraining)¶
The automatically exported _training.pdf summarizes each training stage (median and interquartile range across branch models). To inspect individual Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 model curves, run the following optional cell. This only plots history already stored in result.uns["navieco_training"].


















In [9]:






# Optional visualization: one figure per trained model; does NOT rerun CONCORD.
model_pdf = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{RESULT_H5AD.stem}_training_by_model.pdf"
nv.pl.training_report(result, detail="models", save=model_pdf, show=False)
print(f"Saved per-model training report: {model_pdf}")

























Saved per-model training report: /charite-store-f/f-bih-pancan_icb_atlas_2026/6.scRNA_Recovery1/6.1.NAViECO_Layer0_user_test/output/PMID42679812_3cohorts_subset_NAViECO_fine_training_by_model.pdf



























Interpreting the outputs correctly¶
Level 0 ≠ Layer 1: navieco_level3 labels are fine cell types; NAViECO Layer 1 transcriptional cell-state recovery is not part of the public 0.1.0a2 API.

Global vs branch UMAPs: the global Level 1 embedding is shared for colouring all label levels; each branch Level 2/3 model has its own latent space and UMAP. Separate branch plots are not spatially or mathematically aligned.

Confidences ≠ validation: reported prediction confidence is not calibrated correctness, and reference-validation accuracy is not Query accuracy.

Reuse without retraining: reopening RESULT_H5AD with anndata.read_h5ad() lets you inspect predictions and existing reports without running nv.annotate() again.


For bugs or feature requests, see the NAViECO GitHub issues.
